engine_status: Global output requires a fresh campaign; local Thames mechanism confirmed by user.

raster.accepted_cut_adjacencies_note: Land neighbours the researched channel separates where no single water tile borders both banks for a crossing (Po, Neckar, Xi River); units cross at the neighbouring crossings. Any other cut fails the navigation checks.

overrides.reason: Natural cataract belt between Matadi and Pool Malebo; bounding envelope conservatively includes rapids.
Falls at the upstream end of the middle Congo navigation.
Cataract belt: retain discontinuity rather than permit fleets across rapids. Broad conservative exclusion, not individual cataract survey.
Natural upper Mississippi navigation break; modern locks excluded.
Natural falls; no modern Welland canal.
Thames cargo navigation corridor; upstream reaches require maintenance and later navigation works. All-fleet use is an engine compromise.
Existing southern Grand Canal and connected maintained waterways; navigation works placed from the existing improvement allowance.
Natural complete navigation barrier; modern canal proposals excluded.

hydroatlas.role: Modern physical river network and discharge proxies; not historical navigability.

etopo.role: Coarse natural gradient proxy; riverbed and individual rapids not resolved.

grand_canal_icomos.role: Huitong 1289 and Tonghui late thirteenth century; chronology of changing courses.

british_canals.role: Exeter 1566, later seventeenth/eighteenth-century canal development; do not pre-place industrial networks.

thames_history.role: Historical port and river access; local fleet abstraction remains a design choice.

congo_1911.role: Pre-major-dam description of natural navigation breaks; not 1300 infrastructure evidence.

nile_1911.role: Cataracts and seasonality; broad natural barrier proxy.

mississippi_nps.role: Natural Saint Anthony Falls and much later navigation engineering.

niagara_nps.role: Natural waterfall barrier, documented by the US National Park Service.

mekong_mrc.role: Natural complete barriers and limited navigation through rapids, shoals and sharp bends.

congo_world_bank.role: Extensive navigable basin waterways coexist with seasonal limitations and cataract barriers; not evidence of 1300 infrastructure.

amazon_dnit.role: Long-distance natural navigation on the Amazon-Solimoes; modern information informs physical capability, not medieval port or dredging infrastructure.

reaches.note: 2026-09-26: navigable rivers come from researched heads of navigation (one JSON per world region, sources inside), traced along vanilla river lines; selection, tropical and override screens below are unused in this mode, the hydrology only annotates discharge and relief.

vanilla_look.note: 2026-10-03 (EU5 1.4 draws rivers in many map modes and animates their flow): visual only. The final rivers are redrawn on vanilla's own river lines and widths (river_vanilla_look.py); the drawing's own rivers stay only where vanilla draws none (farther than cover_pixels, not mostly within duplicate_pixels of a vanilla line) and join vanilla's network. Every ownable location keeps its river level: wider vanilla pixels are capped to the level, level 2 is drawn at width 6 (looks like vanilla's 5), and a location whose visible river is still below its level gets a two-pixel carrier inside the engine's source fade-in (not drawn).

limits: Heads of navigation and obstacles come from researched historical evidence (see configs/navigation_reaches).
All fleet classes can use converted sea zones; barriers (falls, cataracts) are impassable.
Improvable routes are costly but passable until works are completed.
Rivers without a vanilla line follow the drawn export river; canals are straight between stops.
